Build the provenance footnote for a saved figure

Source: R/footnote-provenance.R
provenance_footnote.Rd

Formats the fields save_manuscript() prints below a figure to identify the version of the job that drew it: the commit, the job path, the R, hvtiPlotR and hvtiRtemplates versions and the time, which save_manuscript() joins with a middle dot.

Usage

provenance_footnote(
  commit,
  job,
  versions = .default_versions(),
  time = Sys.time()
)

Arguments

commit

The render commit ID, a single string printed as given: a unique abbreviation, the full ID, or a marker such as "uncommitted".

job

The job path, a single string, such as "30_analyses/survival.qmd".

versions

A named character vector of versions, printed as "<name> <version>" in the order given. The default is R, the installed hvtiPlotR and, when it is installed, hvtiRtemplates.

time

The time of the render, a POSIXct printed as "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M". Default Sys.time().

Value

A character vector of fields: the commit, the job, one field per version and the time. Pass it to the footnote argument of save_manuscript(), which joins and fits it.

Details

The commit comes first, so the shortest line that survives a crop still finds the render record, which names the job. It is printed as given and never shortened here: hvtiPlotR cannot know which abbreviation is unique in the study's repository, so pass one that git verified, such as the output of git rev-parse --short, or the full ID. A marker the caller uses when no commit could be made, such as "uncommitted", prints whole too.

Only the R, hvtiPlotR and hvtiRtemplates versions are printed; the full package list belongs in the render provenance.

hvtiPlotR does not know about studies or git. It formats the parts it is given; the commit and the job path come from the caller.

See also

save_manuscript(), which prints the note in a strip below the figure.

Examples

provenance_footnote(
  commit   = "3f9c2a1",
  job      = "30_analyses/rfs.explain.long_term_survival.primary.qmd",
  versions = c(R = "4.5.1", hvtiPlotR = "2.8.19", hvtiRtemplates = "1.5.3"),
  time     = as.POSIXct("2026-10-29 14:40")
)
#> [1] "3f9c2a1"                                               
#> [2] "30_analyses/rfs.explain.long_term_survival.primary.qmd"
#> [3] "R 4.5.1"                                               
#> [4] "hvtiPlotR 2.8.19"                                      
#> [5] "hvtiRtemplates 1.5.3"                                  
#> [6] "2026-10-29 14:40"
